newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks climb to record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks climb to record closing high.

text.p: Toronto stocks set a record closing high on Thursday, powered by strong corporate earnings and a favorable interest rate picture.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 22.89 points to 6336.02, erasing the last record closing high of 6332.87 set on March 10.
Trading was brisk with turnover of 97 million shares worth C$1.6 billion ($1.2 billion).
Advancing stocks outpaced declines 523 to 444, with 286 issues unchanged.
"The earnings just keep coming in a lot of cases better than expected. For the time being I think all we have to do is sit back enjoy it," said Bill Ram, a Montreal-based stock analyst.
Canada's six major banks are set to report stronger second quarter earnings next week. Bank of Montreal and Toronto Dominion Bank will kick off the profit parade on Tuesday.
Ram said equity markets are also enjoying some relief from the recent volatility over interest rates.
Canadian interest rates are expected to remain low after the U.S. Federal Reserve held U.S. steady earlier this week.
Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Chuck Freedman said on Thursday the central bank would like to close the gap between production capacity and current output and keep inflation low.

"We think 1997 is going to be a good year for (Canadian) growth, it will take up the slack," Freedman said. "We think 1998 will have considerable momentum as well and slack will be gradually taken up over that period," he said.
* Moore Corp Ltd. jumped 1.20 to 30.20 on 897,000 shares after the company said 12.9 million shares were tendered to its share buyback offer.

* Hudson's Bay Co. fell 0.25 to 28.25 on 48,000 shares despite reporting narrower first quarter losses. The department store retailer said on Thursday it hoped to acquire 36 stores from Kmart Canada and 10 Eaton's outlets.
